the_blocking_fact.headline: The tag is no longer missing — the confirmations are. A click can attribute now; what is still blocked is everything that needs owner-side evidence.
the_blocking_fact.detail: Amazon requires Associates tags to be embedded in the product links on the site declared in the application, and it reviews an application only once at least three qualifying sales have been driven within the first 180 days. On 2026-11-17 the owner supplied tracking ID shopnow047c-20 and it is now embedded in every validated Special Link this site publishes, each marked rel=sponsored and disclosed, with one destination check per product passed in the owner's enrolled workflow — so a click can attribute a qualifying purchase. What remains: the five supplied short links themselves carry no tag and their compliance status is unresolved (never 'invalid'), the intended product behind each code is unconfirmed and two of the five currently open meat-thermometer listings (F-42), the tracking-report check needs the owner's Associates Central session (F-43), and no click is collected until the analytics sink is deployed (MI-01). Conversion reporting, the optimizer, and API enrolment that would let the site publish prices and ratings still sit behind those owner-side confirmations.

what_is_settled: The five supplied links resolve, on dated reads across sessions, to stable listings: B04G1MEwY to a Chefman 6-quart dual basket, B02NbDxp3 to an Emeril Lagasse 26-quart French-door oven, B00hJ57DV to a Chefman 8-quart basket fryer, and B0c8moW59 and B0f3GKalj to two meat thermometers (BR-19, BR-20, BR-21, and the S61–S64 reads).
The evidence discipline holds at scale: 152 of 152 pages carry the disclosure, no page prints a product price, and every specification row links to the page it was read from.
The machinery is trustworthy: 45 of 45 workflow steps pass locally, and the counts that matter are derived from the tree rather than typed.
The rules are known and quoted: what may be published, what may not, and where the disclosure has to sit.
what_is_not_settled: Whether the five listings are the products the brief meant. Nothing in any official document binds a supplied code to a product (BQ-18); the product-intent record's intended fields stay blank until the owner states them (F-42).

Whether the account behind the supplied tag matches the declared site and marketplace (BQ-14, BQ-19) — the owner supplied tracking ID shopnow047c-20 on 2026-11-17, but nothing has been read from Associates Central itself (F-43).
Which of the 16 published surfaces is the site that would be declared (BQ-15).
Who writes it, under what name, and whether that name is public (BQ-16).
What readers are searching for. There is no demand signal anywhere in the project, so no topic on the topics board can be ranked by expected volume (BQ-20).

decide_first.why: Declaring one site determines what every other change is a change to. It is also the only decision that has to be right before an application names a URL, because an application is not reassessed after a rejection.
Supplying the Associates tag is the owner's one action that unblocks the entire revenue side. It takes one sign-in and no code.
It costs under an hour and it is reversible. The T55 rebuild removed the phrase from every reader-facing page; 14 operator and companion pages still carry it.

the_one_thing: If only one thing happens next, it should be the owner's confirmation of what each supplied link was meant to promote — the intended ASIN per code, with the date and source of that confirmation. The tag is in; the product-intent record's intended fields are the last blanks keeping this site from stating what it links to.
